target_customer: Online community organizers and creators who want a shared token for their members
problem: Creating and distributing an Ethereum token for a community required technical skill and fees, so communities could not easily run their own currency.
business_model: Free token creation tool with Ethereum network fees; the founder described token creation as a one-time purchase in launch discussion

founders.name: John Palmer
founders.background_notes: The YC page and TechCrunch name only John Palmer. A cypherhunter profile calls him a Hexel co-founder who later worked on PartyDAO; no other co-founder is named, and no education or prior employers were found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapping standard Ethereum token contracts and airdrops in a simple web interface was well within a two person team, though gas handling was fiddly per TechCrunch testing.

defensibility.rationale: Token contracts were open standards and the tool could be copied in weeks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found. The ICO market the product sat beside faced tightening regulation later in 2018, per general reporting not opened here.

market_need_then: Interest in tokens and ICOs was at a peak in early 2018. Hexel pitched community currencies without an ICO, but no usage or revenue figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used onhexel.com, a prefixed domain, per the company URL in the YC directory. The domain no longer resolved in this session.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful pitch on Product Hunt that tokens can be given away for fun

branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt on 2018-02-14, on Hacker News as Launch HN, and covered by TechCrunch on 2018-03-05.

brand_strength.rationale: Short but near identical to the unrelated Hexcel and several Hexel trademarks, and no brand pages or community beyond launch coverage were found.

outcome_analysis: The YC directory marks Hexel inactive, but no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The founder later worked on PartyDAO per a profile. The product rode the early 2018 token boom with no moat and a free pricing model, which are plausible risks but are not stated by any source.
notes: The company site did not resolve (DNS error), so it is treated as dead. The 120K round rests on CB Insights and BounceWatch, which agree on one 120K round; CB Insights also states 1.49M over 3 rounds, an unexplained gap. VCBacked places the company in New York while others say San Francisco. No dated competitor near the batch was found; the BounceWatch list is auto generated and was not used. Launch HN page was not read (redirect).
